text:
nina: thinking about exposing a tiny runtime "knob" for tenants to opt into cheaper routing during off-hours. main trade: compile-time policy variants (cheap/normal/premium) vs runtime scale. thoughts?

carlos: compile-time variants = simple auditing + A/B, but variants explode. runtime knobs better for live signals (queueing, node health) without recompile.

anya: ops concerns: 1) explainability (why route X was chosen) and 2) safety (tenants' cheap mode shouldn't hurt others). runtime must be bounded by compiled guardrails.

kevin: hybrid proposal: compiler emits normalized base_scores and per-tenant floor/ceiling for runtime adjustments. runtime can only apply scale within [floor, ceiling] and must attach compiled_snapshot id to traces. keeps replayability.

nina: we should avoid heavy per-request math; runtime op = single scalar multiply + early hard-constraint checks.

ops-bot: experiment "probe-driven-weighting" live in us-east-1. dashboard -> https://grafana.company/board/probe-drive

carlos: also need consistent units across scorers and model variants. compile-time should normalize scorer ranges (percentile clipping or z-norm) so runtime scales make sense.

anya: fairness: compiler must enforce inter-tenant caps tied to SLA. e.g., basic-tier tenant ceiling cannot exceed 0.3 relative weight in overload. runtime sees cap but cannot override it.

kevin: tracing fields: compiled_snapshot=sha256:abcd..., runtime_scale=0.62, adjustment_reason="offhours". persist in request event and decision log.

nina: draft plan:
1) Compiler outputs: normalized scorers, hard constraints, per-tenant floor/ceiling, compiled_snapshot id.
2) Runtime surface: small allowlist API: { knob: "defer_to_cheap", scale: 0.0-1.0, reason: string } that must fit in [floor, ceiling].
3) Sidecar shim: implement overlay in sidecar first; intercept chooser decisions and apply scale before selection for safe rollback.

carlos: microbench sidecar vs in-process path. watch increased RPC hops. target <2% p50 latency hit.

kevin: also add compile-time lint: flag tenant caps that violate global fairness invariants. treat as policy push failure.

anya: test matrix: numeric stability unit tests, sim with mixed traffic, 1% tenant canary, emergency kill switch to disable runtime scaling.

nina: example compiled payload to include in RFC:
"compiled_snapshot: sha256:abcd1234; scorers: [latency:0.7, cost:0.35]; constraints: {blacklist:[model-x], min_weight:0.1}; tenant_caps: {acme: floor:0.5, ceiling:0.9}"

kevin: perf owner volunteer: i'll run microbench and sim. carlos: telemetry hooks.

carlos: telemetry: emit decision event with compiled_snapshot, runtime_scale, score_delta histogram to detect bias spikes.

anya: rollout: feature-flag per-region, start canary tenants, monitor fairness and unit-cost for 48h, auto-revert if cross-tenant fairness drops >5%.

nina: i'll write RFC with payload examples, lint rules, and checklist. thanks!

ops-bot: created ticket infra/arch-3325001234 -> RFC draft requested.
